report.source_text: Routine blood examination showed a normal haemoglobin level (119 g/L), normal white cell count (5.85×109/L) but severe thrombocytopenia (3000/mm3). Peripheral smear showed normal morphology of red blood cells, leucocytes but significantly reduced platelets. No blast cells or atypical cells were seen. Liver and kidney function tests were within normal limits. Coagulation profile (prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and international normalised ratio (INR)) was normal. Fibrinogen level was slightly elevated (411 mg/dL; range 162–401 mg/dL) but serum triglyceride (55 mg/dL) and serum ferritin (350 ng/mL) were within normal limits. Pro-calcitonin levels were also within normal limits.

report.source_text: On examination, she was alert and playful. Her vitals were stable. Several pinpoint and round to oval (>1 cm) reddish-purple spots were seen on the skin over neck, shoulder, arms and legs. These lesions were not raised and non-blanching suggestive of petechiae and purpura (figure 1). There were no other bleeding manifestations. The rest of the systemic examination was normal.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) secondary to SARS-CoV-2
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 5.5-year-old girl with a history of B-cell ALL on maintenance therapy developed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Twenty-two days after recovery, she presented with widespread non-blanching petechiae and purpura. Laboratory tests revealed severe isolated thrombocytopenia (platelets 3000/mm3) with normal hemoglobin, white cell counts, coagulation profile, and organ function tests. Peripheral smear showed no blast or atypical cells. Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy showed normocellular marrow with increased megakaryopoiesis and no blasts, ruling out leukemia relapse. Autoimmune and infectious serologies were negative. She was treated with platelet transfusion for cutaneous bleeding. These findings confirmed isolated immune-mediated thrombocytopenia consistent with ITP secondary to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
